purpose: Direct Mock (k6 -> Mock LLM directly, no Gateway) open-model (constant-arrival-rate) control calibration.

rates.note: custom client_stream_duration_seconds Trend metric showed p95=104.9s / max=104.965s (JS-side Date.now() read skew, see SUMMARY.md), but k6's own built-in iteration_duration/http_req_duration metrics (Go-runtime-timed, more authoritative) were normal for ALL 901 iterations (avg=7.85s, max=8.09s) -- classified CLEAN based on the authoritative built-in metric, not the skewed custom one
k6 peak CPU 97% -- near single-core saturation, a LOADGEN warning sign for rates beyond this candidate range, though this run itself completed clean

SAFE_OPEN_MAX_basis: robust_clean_ceiling_R (320, top of initial candidate list, no failures/degradation) / 1.25
measurement_tooling_finding: Custom JS-computed Trend metrics (client_stream_duration_seconds, client_ttfc_seconds) in load-test-k6/scenarios/03-constant-arrival-rate-continuous.js can show large transient outliers under high-VU host contention (observed once, R=20) that do NOT reflect actual request/network duration -- k6's own built-in iteration_duration/http_req_duration metrics stayed normal throughout the same run. Recommend cross-checking against built-in metrics during Unit 7+ Open screening/Formal rather than trusting only the custom Trend metrics in isolation.
little_law_sanity_check_R320: R=320 * W~7.8s =~ 2496 expected concurrent in-flight -- used as sanity expectation only per Unit 1 design brief section 18, not as a capacity determinant
